All other files: HEAD inventory via rg, no full reads
method: Inventory via `rg -n 'pub (fn|struct|enum|use|mod|type|const|static|trait)' src/extension/`; consumer/producer parity via `rg -n '<symbol>' src/` per candidate; HEAD-only reads on files >5K (mod.rs / loader.rs / watcher.rs / plugin_state.rs / service_manager.rs / hooks/executor.rs / manifest/parsers.rs / manifest/toml_types.rs / registry/types.rs); TODO/FIXME/XXX/HACK sweep returned 0 hits across src/extension/. Form-5 sweep via `rg -n 'Ok\(\(\)\)' src/extension/` followed by context reads.

findings.rationale: Defined as a public method but `rg -n 'stop_watcher' src/` returns only the definition site. No internal call, no external handler. The watcher is started exactly once at boot via `start_watcher` (mod.rs:889, wired to start/mod.rs:2568) and never stopped — the manager shuts down with the process. A `stop_watcher` API has been planned and never wired. Pure orphan.
findings.residual_risk: Low; if process exit ever needs to be mid-flight graceful, this stub would be useful, but a server-scope Stop RPC does not exist today so the cut is safe.

findings.rationale: Builder-style setter defined as `pub fn with_memory_registry(self, ...) -> Self`. `rg -n 'with_memory_registry' src/` returns only the definition. The doc immediately above already concedes: 'For use before the manager is shared behind an `Arc`. If you already have `Arc<ExtensionManager>`, use `set_memory_registry` instead.' The boot path in start/mod.rs uses `set_memory_registry` (tool_catalog_init.rs:470) and never holds an `ExtensionManager` by value. The builder takes `self` rather than `&mut self`, so it would also conflict with the `&Arc<ExtensionManager>` usage inside the manager itself.
findings.residual_risk: Very low; only useful for callers who construct `ExtensionManager` by value before sharing — there are none.

findings.consumer_location: none (writer and reader are both internal to mod.rs)
findings.rationale: Doc on the field (mod.rs:237) claims `Exposed via Self::reload_count — used by integration tests to assert at-most-once reload behaviour on adjacent watcher events, and available for future runtime observability.` `rg -n 'reload_count' src/` returns only the four sites inside mod.rs itself — no integration test or production caller reads it. The doc claim is stale (Form 4: producer documented as wired but unwired).
findings.residual_risk: Trivial; the field is unused and the atomic increment on every reload is a negligible cost. Doc must be updated when the field is cut.

findings.produced: ExtensionManager skill_ops API (get_skill, get_command, get_agent, get_all_skills, get_all_agents, get_primary_agents, get_sub_agents, invoke_skill_tool, execute_skill, execute_command, aleph_home)
findings.rationale: Of the eleven `ExtensionManager` methods declared in skill_ops.rs, only `get_all_commands` (skill_ops.rs:32, wired to tool_catalog_init.rs:178) and `skill_system` (skill_ops.rs:173, wired to tool_catalog_init.rs:157) have any production caller. `rg -n 'ExtensionManager::(invoke_skill_tool|execute_skill|execute_command|aleph_home|get_skill|get_command|get_agent|get_all_skills|get_all_agents|get_primary_agents|get_sub_agents)' src/` returns zero hits. They were the old 'query the registry for tools/skills/agents' surface and got superseded by `active_plugin_tools_snapshot()` (mod.rs:1276), `plugin_agent_to_def` (mod.rs:236), and the `SkillSystem` scanner projection (projection.rs).
findings.residual_risk: Low; no internal Rust caller, but if any external binding ever wanted `ExtensionManager.get_skill(...)` it is silently missing. The `SkillSystem` twin is the documented replacement.

findings.rationale: The `adapter_registry` field is used internally (mod.rs:572, mod.rs:1334), but the public getter `ExtensionManager::adapter_registry(&self) -> &AdapterRegistry` has zero callers. `rg -n '\.adapter_registry' src/` returns the two internal field reads plus the getter itself. The getter exposes the registry for 'future runtime observability' that never arrived.

`pub fn add_watch_dir(&self, dir: PathBuf) -> Result<()>` is defined but `rg -n '\.add_watch_dir\(' src/` returns zero callers. The watcher is constructed with either a fixed dir set via `new_with_dirs` (watcher.rs:167, used by mod.rs:980) or the default set via `new` (watcher.rs:132). Post-construction dir-adding was never wired.

All three are only used by tests inside service_manager.rs itself (`rg` shows 14 internal test references, zero external). `ExtensionManager` exposes its own `running_service_count()` and `list_services()` (service_ops.rs:227, 216), which are wired to the gateway services handler, so the lower-level `ServiceManager` accessors are pure test scaffolding leaking through `pub`.
findings.residual_risk: Trivial; demoting to `pub(crate)` or `#[cfg(test)]` is a one-line cleanup.

findings.rationale: `rg -n 'extension::manifest::validate_plugin_name' src/` returns zero hits; the only invocation is the test in the same module. Compare with `validate_plugin_id` (mod.rs:108), which is wired through hooks/executor.rs:581 and hooks/mod.rs:456. `validate_plugin_name` was added speculatively; its check ('non-empty, lowercase-kebab, starts with letter') is duplicated by `sanitize_plugin_id` at the adapter boundary.
findings.residual_risk: Low; if a future caller wants a stricter human-readable name check it could be resurrected, but the silent gap has lasted long enough to count as dead.

findings.consumer_location: none in production (re-exported at mod.rs:71 but never imported; only consumed by tests inside capability.rs)
findings.rationale: `rg -n 'CapabilitySource\b|SourceFormat\b' src/` returns only the definition and the in-file tests. Registry types use `DiscoverySource` (registry/types.rs:227, 326), not `CapabilitySource`. `SourceFormat` enumerates Aleph/ClaudeCode/Codex/Cursor/AutoDiscovered/Runtime but no field anywhere carries it. Both are pub-re-exported from `extension::*` (mod.rs:71) yet zero downstream consumers — neither by full path nor by re-export.
findings.residual_risk: Low; both are stable Serialize/Deserialize tuples that are cheap to revive when a registration row actually needs to carry origin/format metadata.

findings.rationale: The doc-comment claim is `[is_extension_manager_initialized] contributes **0** of those [production call sites]: its only five callers live in gateway/handlers/plugins/handlers/tests.rs`. Counting actual call sites with `rg -n 'is_extension_manager_initialized' src/`: 1 in extension/hooks/executor.rs:1516, 5 in gateway/handlers/services.rs (498, 516, 540, 564, 593), plus the 5 in tests. So the comment understates the production count by 7. This is Form 4 (name/path drift between a written description and the actual code). The doc also undergirds a downstream assertion in `manager_global::tests` (line 96) and a `MissingSemantics::ConsumerDecides` classification in `census.rs`. The classification is sound (each consumer handles absence differently), but the cited count is wrong. A doc fix is required; the call sites themselves are correctly wired.
findings.residual_risk: The mis-cited number is the kind of thing a future reader will trust when re-classifying the slot — they will be wrong by 7.

notes: The extension module is unusually well-instrumented: every orphan surfaced here has either a doc comment claiming a use that no longer exists (Form 4: `manager_global.rs` `is_extension_manager_initialized` doc, `mod.rs` `reload_count` doc, `mod.rs` `with_memory_registry` doc) or a dead public method (Form 1: `stop_watcher`, `with_memory_registry`, `adapter_registry`, `add_watch_dir`, `ServiceManager::{clear,running_count,total_count}`, the skill_ops block). The codebase does NOT have a grep-diff guard for `pub fn`s in this module — the same fact (the orphan method exists) is replicated only by doc comments, which drift. A `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` build is green today because the orphan methods are `pub` (clippy's dead_code lint does not fire on pub items). The cheap follow-up is either (a) delete the methods, or (b) downgrade them to `pub(crate)` / `#[cfg(test)]` so clippy flags them. The Form-5 sweep was clean — every `Ok(())` I followed either documented its inertness (`CapabilityApi::dispatch` McpServer arm) or carried a real side effect (cache writes, registrations). The TODO/FIXME/XXX/HACK sweep returned 0 hits across src/extension/, which matches the codebase-wide pattern of using prose comments instead — the prose itself is where doc drift lives, and finding sw-extension-4-1 is the canonical example.
